The Prophet sent a letter that Chosroes tore up, and because rulers read only sealed letters he had a silver ring engraved 'Muhammad Allah's Messenger'.
A Jewess brought the Prophet a poisoned sheep and he ate of it; he refused to have her killed, and Anas kept seeing the poison's effect in his mouth.
The Prophet hid behind date-palms to overhear Ibn Saiyad, but his mother alerted him, and the Prophet said he would otherwise have revealed his reality.
Asked on his Hajj where he will stay, the Prophet asks whether Aqil left them any house and names Khaif Bani Kinana, where Quraish swore to boycott Bani Hashim.
Inspired at forty, the Prophet in Mecca tells the persecuted Khabbab earlier believers endured worse; Uqba lays entrails on him and throttles him, and the first converts were few.
Setting out for Hunain, the Prophet plans to camp at Khaif Bani Kinana, where the pagans swore to boycott Banu Hashim.
Ka'b bin Malik, Jabir and his uncles attended the Aqaba pledge, where, Ubada says, they pledged to worship Allah alone and avoid theft, illegal sexual intercourse, killing and slander.
The Prophet sends a letter to Khosrau through the governor of Bahrain; Khosrau tears it up, and the Prophet is reported to have invoked Allah to tear them to pieces.
The Prophet spent ten years in Mecca receiving the Quran and ten in Medina, died aged sixty-three, and at his death his armor was mortgaged to a Jew for barley.
Asked the worst thing the pagans did to the Prophet, Abdullah bin Amr tells how Uqba throttled him at the Ka'bah until Abu Bakr pushed him away.
Abu Jahl threatens to tread on the Prophet's neck if he sees him praying at the Ka'bah, and the Prophet says the angels would snatch him away.
